arrival.environment: Strong exterior establishing shot: the central entry and Pavilion title read immediately; teal uprights and coral trim establish a coherent theatrical palette. Railings, ramp, stairs, glazing and foliage compete around the lower-right circulation routes. The window interiors and trees dissolve into many small transitional colors at 4×.
arrival.narrative: The restroom pictogram and directional arrow support the approach. The locked prose names EXPERIENCE YOURSELF and PUBLIC RESTROOMS; the image abbreviates these to the Pavilion title and pictograms. Treat this as economical signage, not a spelling defect or a mandate to add more tiny text. The shared arrival master appropriately avoids committing to one incoming route.
arrival.characters: No human NPC is visible. This is an environment-density issue rather than a portrait-detail issue.
arrival.grid: The title is comparatively firm; shrubs, reflected interiors and handrail edges are noticeably softer. Rebuild selected edges and group foliage into larger masses while preserving the composition.
arrival.comparisonText: The Bureau makes its closed doors and one foreground notice dominant, with secondary garden detail behind glazing. Arrival needs that hierarchy around the entry, not the Bureau's exact colors.
arrival.next: Retain camera, building proportions, main title and directional cues. Refine glazing, foliage and rail contours in bounded regions only; no full redraw is justified by this successful layout.

backstage.environment: The corridor has a useful clear center and converging teal beams, but wall and floor stippling overwhelm the ordinary backstage mood. Cable loops, leaning scenery and scattered papers have frayed boundaries. The small mechanical clapper reads less decisively than the exit. This is the largest visible break in material treatment from the reference family.
backstage.narrative: Scenery, cables, sandwich, discarded papers, clapper and a plain daylight exit are present. The carton labels and overturned podium are not clearly readable as those specific props. Prioritize their silhouettes; the script can carry long carton text. The tiny EXIT sign is weak at native size. The restroom pictogram across the courtyard supports the final beat.
backstage.characters: No human NPC. Keep the clapper visibly a mounted mechanism; its recently approved correction deliberately removed character-like anatomy.
backstage.grid: 91.92% of pixels have no exactly matching orthogonal neighbor under the audit's RGB diagnostic. The visible mottled concrete and fuzzy cable contours corroborate the metric; the number alone does not establish poor authorship.
backstage.comparisonText: Tour Tram also uses a deep corridor with repeating ceiling fixtures and floor planes. Its grouped materials and firm seat silhouettes keep the passage readable despite surface texture.
backstage.next: Reconstruct at 314×206 from the existing composition reference. Use broad concrete planes, economical cable loops, distinct crate/cart silhouettes, a clearly mechanical clapper and a readable EXIT. Retain the unglamorous daylight escape; no new human or extra story beat.

courtesy_stage.environment: The shutter over the original opening and the displaced frame to the left communicate a changed restroom state. The bench, relocated frame, track and spotlight are tightly packed, making the movement path harder to parse than the main door itself. The established coral/teal room remains coherent.
courtesy_stage.narrative: The hidden rail, closed inner shutter and spotlight represent the courtesy demonstration. The door-holding visitor and the narrated movement of the attendant are absent from this static master. This weakens the human joke but does not by itself establish a missing required state or authorize new art. A shared tableau cannot depict every moment.
courtesy_stage.characters: The seated attendant retains recognizable side-parted dark hair, glasses, cream shirt and teal vest. The tiny smile, eyes and clasped fingers use more facial/hand detail than Reception. His calm seated pose provides little support for the alarmed dialogue.
courtesy_stage.grid: Mixed treatment: some shutter and trim lines read cleanly, while the face, spotlight falloff, bench seams and rail have many intermediate shades.
courtesy_stage.comparisonText: The Bureau separates its blocked door and readable notice from the foreground desk. Courtesy should similarly separate the rail, displaced jamb and blocked opening through value and overlap.
courtesy_stage.next: Clarify the track and frame depth order; simplify the attendant's face and hands without changing his scale. A visitor silhouette or action pose would need separate scoped creative approval. Preserve the established restroom topology and already-approved close portrait.

exit_vestibule.environment: The denied fixtures on the left and descending exit route on the right form a clear two-part composition. Strong uprights, a readable EXIT arrow and visible glass establish the puzzle. The ramp mouth sits beside a large restroom pictogram and can initially read as another entrance. Pipes, sink edges and handrails are somewhat soft.
exit_vestibule.narrative: Fixtures, gate and smooth descending ramp support door_dash_pass. The simultaneous cutaway-like view of restroom and ramp is an inferred architectural arrangement, not proof that the room is physically impossible. The script does not provide a floor plan to resolve this with certainty.
exit_vestibule.characters: No NPC is visible. The maintenance worker is part of the later narrated destination, so adding him to this view is unnecessary.
exit_vestibule.grid: Large teal planes remain legible despite source-derived shading. Ramp lighting and rail edges carry finer transitions than the Chapter 2 reference.
exit_vestibule.comparisonText: Control Tower uses repeated furniture, window framing and clear floor planes to distinguish work areas. Vestibule has comparable value separation, but its intended route needs a spatial continuity decision rather than a palette-only repair.
exit_vestibule.next: Retain this selection pending a small floor-plan/camera check against restroom entrance and scanner. Nate should decide whether the two-part view reads clearly in sequence. Do not commission a redraw for an unproven topology problem.

exterior_exit.environment: The closed loading shutter, empty padded cart and spare cushions provide three clear silhouettes, with an unobstructed foreground. Pavilion trim, glazing and planting match Arrival. The empty cart is at a believable architectural scale and communicates a harmless ejection.
exterior_exit.narrative: This is a truthful common exterior for three safe endings; it avoids baking one transient ribbon, protagonist or human-chain action into all routes. The loading-door/cart emphasis favors PERFECTLY SAFE, but the same exterior remains usable for the other exits.
exterior_exit.characters: No human is shown. No protagonist face, duplicate or portrait-like NPC is introduced.
exterior_exit.grid: Foliage, glass and cushion shading retain softness, but the cart, shutter and floor remain readable at native and 4×. Residual processing is accepted here because it does not materially obscure the story objects.
exterior_exit.comparisonText: Moving Forest is far denser, yet distinguishes important trunks and travel routes with broad silhouettes. Exterior Exit achieves the same object/path separation with fewer elements.
exterior_exit.next: Leave untouched. Global recoloring or palette reduction would risk a successful scene for little practical gain.

human_verification_stage.environment: Clear theater staging: camera left, presenter beside a marked platform, central thirty-second display and restroom reveal right. The scene communicates the demonstration before close reading. Curtain folds, stand hardware and soft platform edging slightly weaken the otherwise deliberate geometry.
human_verification_stage.narrative: Camera, marked circle and countdown support the initial verification and later dialogue. A static thirty-second master cannot show all subsequent screen messages or platform movements. That reuse is documented; do not turn this audit into a new state inventory.
human_verification_stage.characters: Auburn bob, coral blouse, slate jacket/skirt and open-hand gesture match the approved presenter portrait. Her head, tiny mouth/eyes, jacket seams and hand are more softly described than Reception's scene figure. Her stage scale is plausible; enlarging her would worsen the camera relationship.
human_verification_stage.grid: The display numerals have firmer discrete shapes than the face and silhouette. Character contours and curtain folds should use a more consistent cluster vocabulary.
human_verification_stage.comparisonText: Control Tower provides a good hierarchy for a room with several machines: consolidate each device into a strong mass, then reserve small details for the important controls.
human_verification_stage.next: Keep the camera and platform layout. Refine the presenter into clear hair, face, coral neckline and slate costume masses; use one hand shape rather than individual fingers. Clean the stage ellipse and microphone separation locally.

locomotion_stage.environment: The added orange padded pit, safety net, moving-floor arrow, platform rim and microphone form a crowded central machine. Net lines cross the display support area and the pit rim has uneven stair-step/perspective cues. The broad theater shell is successful; the demonstrated mechanism is much less immediately readable.
locomotion_stage.narrative: The pit and net are present, but the relation between moving surface, stationary landing and backstage escape is harder to infer than the locked text suggests. A reconstruction should clarify those three surfaces without enlarging or redesigning the room.
locomotion_stage.characters: The presenter retains the same bob/coral/slate identity and plausible standing scale. Facial and jacket microdetail remains soft; the near-unchanged open-hand pose gives little sense of celebrating a locomotion demonstration. Stronger gesture can be conveyed with arm angle and silhouette alone.
locomotion_stage.grid: Thin net lines and several narrow parallel machine boundaries compete at the logical grid. This is a compositional/shape problem as well as source softness; a global palette cap would not resolve it.
locomotion_stage.comparisonText: Tour Tram describes movement space through an unmistakable aisle, repeated seats and a separate door. Apply that clarity to moving floor, safe pit and fixed exit; do not copy its literal tram geometry.
locomotion_stage.next: Reconstruct the moving apparatus and presenter at native resolution, retaining the existing theater architecture as a reference. Use a few separated net strands, broad padded panels, a coherent rim and an unmistakable stationary landing. Keep the protagonist off-camera.

paper_emergency.environment: The huge paper loops and descending brushes convey absurdity, but several overlapping pale ribbons obscure their attachment and direction. Individual brush bristles, translucent-looking paper transitions and floor tangencies create busy, weakly separated boundaries. The base restroom architecture is still clear.
paper_emergency.narrative: Endless paper, ornamental plant and giant safety brushes are visible. The smiling, clasped-hand attendant and absent visitor do not convey his shouted emergency, ankle snarl or active evacuation. One still need not show every narrated event, but this image's human action undercuts its defining beat.
paper_emergency.characters: Same recognizable attendant as the entrance; retained portrait-like facial marks and interlaced fingers have little value at this scale. A startled head angle, clear bent arm or broad stop gesture would communicate more than additional expression pixels. Preserve the glasses cue and cream/teal costume; do not enlarge him.
paper_emergency.grid: High-contrast paper loops dominate the native view while fuzzy brush fringes and tiny receipt markings provide little useful information at 4×.
paper_emergency.comparisonText: Groundskeeper has substantial mechanical clutter, yet a dominant single machine silhouette and grounded contact points organize it. Paper Emergency needs equally clear paper origin, brush mechanism and evacuation direction.
paper_emergency.next: Reconstruct the emergency action over the established room reference: two or three broad ribbon loops, simple brush masses on readable arms, clear floor contact and a simplified alarmed attendant. Any visitor addition must be specifically included in Nate's later scope; no new portrait is needed.

record_printer.environment: The printer's long receipt provides a strong vertical-to-floor story shape while preserving the door/gate and attendant. Its origin merges with the cream counter/papers and the pale floor loop is less distinct at native size. Environment colors and camera remain consistent with the entrance.
record_printer.narrative: The long printout communicates the record without illegibly reproducing its full text. This master also serves the stapler jam and quiet confession; it does not visibly show those later states. That reuse was previously documented, so new overlays remain a separate creative choice.
record_printer.characters: The attendant's costume and hair agree with the portrait. Detailed smile, lenses, cuffs and finger pattern have less value than a clear head and cream sleeve silhouette. Retaining the same seated figure across changing emotions is a static-master compromise, not a failure of portrait continuity.
record_printer.grid: Paper edge widths and the output slot need deliberate clusters; the face and plant retain the source-derived softness of the shared restroom base.
record_printer.comparisonText: The Bureau uses a light notice against dark doors to make its focal document unmistakable. Here the receipt needs a stronger local value separation from counter and floor, without writing the full record in scene pixels.
record_printer.next: Refine receipt origin, two continuous edge paths and floor-loop spacing. Simplify the tiny attendant face/hands if a shared restroom sprite pass is later approved. Keep the room and all portrait assets.

record_scanner.environment: One of the clearest scene compositions: the closed/slightly open door fills the left, the document roller is an isolated right-hand object, and the green/red reader is plainly visible. Large cream and teal masses keep the important action readable.
record_scanner.narrative: The paper-bearing roller, door and indicator communicate authorization of a document. The attendant is absent from the environment even though dialogue mentions him; the separate alarmed/idle portrait handles identity and expression. No extra scene figure is necessary merely because a portrait exists.
record_scanner.characters: No embedded human. The paper's teal marks read as an abstract record, not an embodied Original, and should stay abstract.
record_scanner.grid: Door shading and slot highlights are softer than the Bureau, but object silhouettes remain robust at both scales. Processing history does not justify replacing this functioning image.
record_scanner.comparisonText: Like the Bureau, Scanner gives the barred access point and one piece of paperwork visual priority. The simpler camera and restrained prop inventory are effective.
record_scanner.next: Leave untouched. Preserve the existing opaque environment and independent attendant portrait/background pairing.

restroom_entrance.environment: A successful foundation: readable RESTROOM sign, real sinks/stalls, inner gate, bench, desk and exit glazing. The room has stable perspective and a coherent coral/teal palette. Soft plant leaves, small fittings and busy attendant facial marks reduce its finish beside Reception.
restroom_entrance.narrative: The real functioning restroom is visibly distinct from a display prop. The passing visitors and some changing reader states are supplied by narration rather than this shared master. Showing green here does not illustrate every red-indicator refusal; flag the tradeoff without inventing state requirements.
restroom_entrance.characters: Hair part, glasses cue, cream shirt and muted teal vest preserve the approved attendant identity. Smile, eyebrow/lens shapes and clasped fingers attempt too much fine description. He is larger on the canvas than Reception's figure because this is a closer room view; that alone does not establish implausible scale.
restroom_entrance.grid: Desk, gate and major wall divisions read well. The face/hand transitions and fine sink hardware look sampled rather than consistently cluster-authored. A prior localized face pass was partly reverted in v08; do not reintroduce its rejected design by rote.
restroom_entrance.comparisonText: The Bureau clarifies denied restroom access through doors, sign and desk masses. Reception shows how to keep a small human legible without a miniature portrait. Both support retaining this room while simplifying the seated figure.
restroom_entrance.next: Use a bounded native sprite/edge refinement, preserving camera, scale, equipment and the approved microphone. Keep the hair shape, cream sleeves, vest and minimal spectacles; merge fingers into a hand mass. Any propagation to related masters needs its own scoped approval.

service_exit.environment: Broad cabinet and pipe masses balance an open daylight door. The light wedge leads directly out; large floor tiles and restrained props keep the passage calm. Teal structure and coral stripe maintain the Pavilion identity without ornamental overload.
service_exit.narrative: The shared service threshold truthfully supports both the presenter's rescue and the attendant's honest exit. Keeping it free of an embedded NPC lets either independent portrait speak without contradictory human staging.
service_exit.characters: No scene figure. The detailed quiet attendant and relieved presenter belong in the close portrait view, which is the desired scene/portrait separation.
service_exit.grid: There is residual shading softness around pipes, plant and door hardware, but it does not compromise the strong cabinet/door silhouettes or the action route.
service_exit.comparisonText: Tour Tram's clear aisle and open door guide the eye through a more complex room. Service Exit achieves that guidance economically with one doorway and a single daylight shape.
service_exit.next: Leave untouched, including its approved tighter portrait background. No need to introduce a small person just to mirror a dialogue layer.

surprise_stage.environment: The raised platform, confetti device and lifted hands establish a comic event. Confetti fragments, the presenter's hand, the cannon and the dark two-dot panel crowd the central focal area. The shell matches Verification and preserves the right-side backstage doorway.
surprise_stage.narrative: Early confetti and a startled presenter support genuine_surprise; the unlocked backstage exit is present. The two pale marks on the central panel are ambiguous without narration. A static image need not carry the certificate and every screen message, but the surprise response should be more immediate.
surprise_stage.characters: The auburn hair and slate/coral outfit remain continuous with the alarmed portrait. Small open-mouth/eye marks and jacket highlights compete with confetti near her face. Keep the elevated-platform scale; simplify face and hair and distinguish both hands as broad silhouettes away from the head and panel.
surprise_stage.grid: The image contains fewer unique colors than several clearer Chapter 3 scenes, illustrating why color count cannot decide the action. The problem is local focal overlap and character-boundary softness.
surprise_stage.comparisonText: Groundskeeper organizes a busy mechanical event around one unmistakable silhouette. Surprise should similarly separate presenter, firing device and panel, keeping confetti a sparse accent.
surprise_stage.next: Local native-cluster refinement of the presenter, hand/head separation, cannon silhouette and selected confetti. Retain camera, platform height, doorway and the approved alarmed portrait; do not rebuild the entire stage.

urgency_stage.environment: Red curtains distinguish the urgency state and focus the central timer/platform. The real restroom reveal stays visible and the single seated visitor is economical. Bright red folds compete somewhat with the presenter and coral rim; stage ellipses retain soft, uneven edges.
urgency_stage.narrative: The bell, curtains, timer and lone visitor support the urgency demonstration. Rotation is not obvious in a still, and the visitor later leaves; a static master is a temporal compromise. Preserve the existing narrative rather than adding large labels to compensate.
urgency_stage.characters: The visitor's dark hair, cream shoulder and seated pose are appropriately simplified and should stay that way; no detailed face is needed. The presenter's identity is correct, but face, bell-hand and jacket marks could be reduced to clearer masses. Her size relative to the room is believable.
urgency_stage.grid: Hard display numerals sit beside softer character edges and curtain shading. A coherent material palette and a few clean folds would improve consistency without losing theatrical color.
urgency_stage.comparisonText: Control Tower separates warm light, dark structure and instrument faces despite detailed surroundings. Urgency should keep its red curtains but lower their internal detail and give the presenter a clearer value boundary.
urgency_stage.next: Refine presenter, bell silhouette, selected curtain folds and platform ellipse. Preserve the already successful simplified visitor. Use any approved Verification sprite treatment as an identity reference, not an automatic copy into this different gesture.
